key_insight: Hierarchical multipoint anchoring strengthens buried interfaces in inverted perovskite solar cells, improving efficiency and resistance to thermal cycling.
engineering_relevance: Engineering adhesion at transparent-conductive-oxide/SAM interfaces offers a route to more durable, high-efficiency perovskite photovoltaics.
method: Pretreat transparent conductive oxides with a homometallic halide to guide ordered self-assembled monolayer (SAM) formation.
Increase surface hydroxyl species to enable multipoint anchoring dominated by metal–oxygen coordination.
Use chloride-induced hydrogen bonding to cooperatively reinforce interfacial anchoring.
evidence_signal: Devices achieved 27.3% efficiency (26.9% certified) and retained 94% of initial efficiency after 400 temperature cycles from −40 to 85 °C under ISOS-T-3.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish whether these gains persist in large-area modules or under combined outdoor stressors.
paper_title: Hierarchical interfacial anchoring for durable perovskite solar cells
